analysis:
The only changed file is docs/operations/provider-release.md, a documentation-only change. It updates the date, adds a cluster-runtime-facts signing step (patch lines 577-579), adds a cluster_runtime_* payload note at ~602-604 and 607-610, and adds content in head lines 649-795 (base units cover 482-770 only). The visible head unit (head lines 1-481) contains only unchanged text with respect to the changed ranges, so the new cluster-runtime-facts section was not visible in supplied head text. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the content of the new payload fields and the section after line 649 were not fully examined.

What I examined: the release pipeline description in the base text (signing, staging, registration, dev-branch lane, secret scoping, ReleaseVersionGreater caveats), and head lines 1-481 (identity table, dev/staging lanes, secret table, source gate). These are descriptive, and no control change is made by this PR. Threat IDs touched conceptually: A-011/A-017 (binary hash registry and build qualifications), T-034/T-054 (signed-build identity), and TB-011. The doc states that official registration does not itself authorize serving, and that runtime Apple verification and matching hashes remain required, which is consistent with the TB-011 and T-054 contracts. There is no code or workflow change in the supplied evidence, so no concrete security regression can be asserted.

Remaining integration questions: whether the new cluster_runtime_* fields registered in POST /v1/releases are verified or merely trusted from pipeline provenance by the coordinator, and whether the cluster helpers signing and attestation path (darkbloom-cluster-worker, network-only entitlements) widens any trust boundary. Those would be in other files and in the truncated doc sections, which were not supplied here.
